description: This dataset gives the dimensions and coordinates of vertical structural elements, walls and columns, for 59 piloti-type reinforced concrete buildings surveyed after the magnitude 5.4 earthquake near Pohang, South Korea, on 11 November 2017, as the record states. It was published on DesignSafe-CI in 2024 by Yunlan Zhang and Lucas Laughery as a re-use of data from drawings in the joint American Concrete Institute and Taiwan NCREE damage survey (Sim et al., 2017), whose team surveyed 74 structures over one week. The record notes peak ground accelerations up to 0.27 g and velocities up to 12 cm/s near the epicentre, and damage to schools and houses. Coverage: 59 soft-storey (piloti) buildings in Pohang. Access: DesignSafe Data Depot, project PRJ-4780. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Creative Commons (licence type not stated in the DataCite rights). Access is free of charge. Caveats: element data come from the survey drawings, not new measurements, and only piloti buildings are included. Simulation uses: studying how element size, shape and location affected the seismic response of soft-storey concrete buildings, and fragility calibration. Related records: the NEES soft-story hybrid test and the STEER reconnaissance series.
